139.signal: "Can the string be cut into dictionary words?" (or how many ways / minimum cuts) → DP over prefixes: dp[i] = the first i characters can be split.
clarify: Can a dictionary word be reused? → Yes, any number of times.
Are the words unique, and is everything lowercase? → Yes to both.
Return a bool, or the actual split? → Just whether a split exists (Word Break II asks for all splits).

ladder.idea: Recursively try every dictionary word as the next piece.
Memoize the recursion on the start index, so each suffix is solved once.
Bottom-up dp[i] over prefixes; only try last words up to the longest dictionary word, and break once dp[i] is True.

139.why: Any valid split of s[:i] ends with some word s[j:i], and what remains, s[:j], must itself be splittable. So dp[i] only depends on smaller prefixes, and bounding j by the longest word length L keeps the inner loop short.
139.dry_run:
`s = "leetcode"`, words `{leet, code}`, L = 4

| i | prefix | last word tried | dp[i] |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | "" | (base) | T |
| 4 | leet | s[0:4] = leet, dp[0] = T | T |
| 8 | leetcode | s[4:8] = code, dp[4] = T | **T** |
tests: Whole string is one word: `"apple"`, `["apple"]` → true
Words that prefix each other: `"catsandog"`, `["cats","dog","sand","and","cat"]` → false
Exponential trap for plain recursion: `"aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaab"`, `["a","aa","aaa"]` → false (must be fast)
bugs: `dp` needs n + 1 slots with `dp[0] = True`; an n-slot array is off by one on the last prefix.
`range(max(0, i - max_len), i)`: forgetting `max(0, …)` makes j negative and silently slices from the end.
Keep `words` a set: `s[j:i] in wordDict` on a list is O(m) per lookup.
followups: Return every sentence (Word Break II) → DFS from each index with memoized lists of sentences.
Minimum number of words → dp[i] = 1 + min over valid j, initialised to infinity.
Very long dictionary words → walk a Trie forward from each reachable index instead of slicing and hashing.
